answer.rationale: The write-path latency spike correlates tightly with the release window (p99 climbing for 90 minutes, release deployed 2 hours ago). Memory b1 documents an analogous case where a rollback cleared a checkout-error spike with zero customer impact and the prior build was stable. Regional failover (memory b2) and circuit breakers (memory b4) address dependency or infra-level faults, not a regression introduced by a code change. Adding capacity or routing to read replicas (memory b5) does not fix a bad build and would delay removing the root cause during peak settlement writes. Rolling back restores the last known-good build, directly removing the suspected regression while preserving in-flight writes; the prior build handled equivalent settlement load on day 18 without issue.
